note.note:
Action Plan:
1) Book in-person appointment with clinic support team for full neurological examination, including fundoscopic exam (to “look at the back of the eyes”), and blood pressure measurement.
2) Start prescribed stronger anti-inflammatory analgesic (similar to ibuprofen; name/dose/route/frequency not documented). Take with food. May take paracetamol/acetaminophen at the same time.
3) Continue current combined oral contraceptive pill for now; reassess suitability after examination. If migraine with aura is confirmed, anticipate changing to a non-estrogen method.
4) Safety net: If headache becomes unbearable, worsens, or changes in character before the appointment, attend the Emergency Department (A&E). Patient may also call the clinic for further advice.
5) Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
- Reason for visit: New “blinding” headache for 3 days, constant; impairs ability to work.
- Headache history:
  - Onset: Sudden upon awakening, 3 days ago; continuous since.
  - Severity: 8/10 at worst; decreases to ~5/10 with ibuprofen but never fully resolves.
  - Location: Diffuse; worse over right eye.
  - Associated symptoms: Photophobia; “shooting lights”/weird visual phenomena; mild nausea without vomiting.
  - Negatives: No focal neurologic symptoms (no numbness, tingling, weakness), no change in smell/taste, no fever, no URI/sinus symptoms, no cough, no epistaxis/hemoptysis.
  - Sleep: Able to sleep; not waking at night; wakes with headache in the morning.
  - Positional elements: Brief stabbing pain when standing quickly; sensation of “something moving” with head thrown back.
- Past medical history: Remote history of unspecified pain when younger; no chronic conditions reported.
- Medications:
  - Combined oral contraceptive pill (started ~1 year ago; exact product not documented; dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Ibuprofen as needed for headache (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Allergies: No known drug allergies.
- Social history: Lives alone; works from home; non-smoker; alcohol about three drinks once weekly; no illicit drug use; no recent travel.
- Family history: Mother has severe migraines with vomiting.
- Recent eye exam: Reported normal.

Objective:
- Examination: None performed (teleconsult).
- Vitals: Not obtained.
- Investigations: None today. Patient reports recent optometry/eye check was normal (no change in vision).

Assessment & Plan:
1. New severe headache with photophobia and visual disturbance (3 days):
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Migraine with aura (possible status migrainosus). Supported by DDx: “Migraine with aura (possible status migrainosus)” – High likelihood.
   - Differential diagnosis (DDx-consistent):
     - Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (Medium): Risk factor of estrogen OCP; new persistent severe headache with visual symptoms; positional sensitivity reported. Opposing: no focal deficits/seizures/papilledema reported.
     - Tension-type headache (Low-Medium): Constant, diffuse pain could fit; opposing migrainous features (photophobia, visual phenomena, nausea).
     - Idiopathic intracranial hypertension (Low): Young woman with headache/visual symptoms; opposing: no papilledema reported, no recumbent worsening/pulsatile tinnitus.
     - Subarachnoid hemorrhage (Low): Acute severe headache with photophobia; opposing: no thunderclap description, no meningismus/neurologic deficits.
   - Investigations planned: In-person neurological examination; fundoscopic exam; blood pressure measurement.
   - Treatment planned: Start stronger NSAID prescribed (name/dose/route/frequency not documented); take with food. May take paracetamol concurrently.
   - Relevant referrals: None today. Safety net provided—attend A&E if worsening, unbearable, or changing before appointment.

2. Combined oral contraceptive use in context of possible migraine with aura:
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Potential estrogen-containing CHC contraindication if migraine with aura is confirmed (DDx item “Medication-induced/worsened migraine from combined hormonal contraceptive” noted under contributors; consistent with discussion).
   - Differential diagnosis: Not applicable (medication risk consideration).
   - Investigations planned: Blood pressure check at upcoming visit.
   - Treatment planned: Continue current pill for now; reassess after examination. If migraine with aura confirmed, plan to switch to a non-estrogen method.
   - Relevant referrals: None discussed today.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: No in-person neurologic exam or fundus exam yet; no vitals including blood pressure; exact OCP name and dosing not documented; ibuprofen dosing not documented. No pregnancy status documented.
- Conflicts between transcript and DDx: None noted.
- Transcript quality: Occasional audio issues/redactions but overall adequate to capture clinical information.
